body.statement:
Define \(U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\).  Then, for every \(n\geq1\) and every \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\),
\[
 ID_G\leq U_2(n),\qquad\text{and therefore}\qquad D_2(n)\leq U_2(n).
\]
This is an unconditional effective-elimination upper bound; it does not assert that \(U_2(n)\) is sharp.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m=n(n+1)/2\) and \(p=|\theta_G|\).  Because \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), the map \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.  The parameter space has dimension \(p\), so its image also has dimension \(p\); since the image lies in the \(m\)-dimensional covariance space,
\[
 p\leq m. \tag{18}
\]
The polynomial ring \(\mathbb Q[\theta_G,s]\) therefore has
\[
 p+m\leq2m=n(n+1) \tag{19}
\]
indeterminates.  By \(\mathrm{lem:cubic\mbox{-}graph\mbox{-}ideal}\), its prime graph ideal \(I_G\) is generated in total degree at most three.

Fix a source coordinate \(q\in\theta_G\) and choose a lexicographic elimination order in which the coordinates \(\theta_G\setminus\{q\}\) precede \(q\), and \(q\) precedes the covariance coordinates.  The cited Gröbner-degree theorem, (19), and \(15/2<8\) bound every element of the reduced Gröbner basis by
\[
 2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{p+m-1}}
 \leq2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{n(n+1)-1}}
 <2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}=U_2(n). \tag{20}
\]

Rational identifiability supplies \(qa(s)-b(s)\in I_G\) with \(a\notin I_G\cap\mathbb Q[s]\).  Reduce \(a\) and \(b\) first by the covariance-only part of the reduced basis.  The leading monomial of the resulting identifying polynomial contains \(q\) and cannot be divided by a covariance-only leading monomial.  The standard elimination argument therefore forces a basis element whose leading monomial has degree one in \(q\), degree zero in every other source coordinate, and whose remaining factors use only \(s\).  It has the form
\[
 q\widetilde a(s)-\widetilde b(s)\in I_G,qquad
 \widetilde a\notin I_G\cap\mathbb Q[s]. \tag{21}
\]
This is exactly the identifying-polynomial extraction from a lexicographic graph-ideal basis.  By (20), the total degree of (21) is at most \(U_2(n)\).  The nonzero class of \(\widetilde a\) cannot vanish on the entire admissible positive-definite parameter domain: that domain is a nonempty Euclidean-open subset of the free source space, and a nonzero polynomial vanishes on no such open set.  Thus (21) is a valid generic certificate.

The argument applies separately to every \(q\in\theta_G\), using no previously identified coordinate.  Ordering these direct certificates arbitrarily gives \(ID_G\leq U_2(n)\).  Maximizing over \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\) proves \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\).
body.justification: The theorem removes the external stopping promise even before the sharp elbow is known.
body.gap: Its doubly exponential-in-an-exponential cutoff is effective rather than sharp.
body.consumer: The exact degree-bounded algorithm receives an unconditional finite cutoff.
